content.overview: Specialist instruction for batch performance, controlled change & handoff within controlled clonal-propagation systems.

sections.title: Measure more than final rooting percentage
sections.body: Useful propagation review can include number started, survival, rooting proportion, timing distribution, loss stage, acclimation loss and handoff count. These measures distinguish where performance changed.

sections.title: Stratify before blaming the protocol
sections.body: Genotype, donor, date, operator, tray position and process version can all structure the data. Comparing those strata helps identify whether an apparent trend is localized or system-wide without converting correlation into causation.

sections.title: Controlled improvement requires a traceable test
sections.body: When evidence supports a process question, change one defined factor under authorized conditions, preserve the comparison and document the decision. A production batch should not become an undocumented experiment.

commonMistakes: Reporting only a final success percentage and losing failure-stage information.
Combining genotypes before checking whether their rooting distributions differ.
Changing several variables together and then claiming one caused the outcome.
content.practicalApplication: Review a multi-batch propagation dataset, identify the strongest supported pattern, state at least one alternative explanation and define a controlled next test plus handoff record.
content.summary: Propagation improvement depends on stratified batch evidence, controlled changes and records that preserve uncertainty as well as results.
